Vimeo allows you to self-distribute short films and charge watchers a small fee. Apparently you keep 90% of the profits after "transaction costs."

I am friends with several people at Vimeo, and a couple of years ago, I sat down with them and talked about what the plans for the future of the site were... At the time, they were growing rapidly and going through a lot of changes, and were unsure about the direction Vimeo was taking.

So I told them some of my ideas. At the time, most were sort of shrugged off as "Yeah, that would be great, BUT...." and they would basically tell me that it was too hard to try anything new.

Well lo and behold, the recent update happens, and everything from PPV to a dedicated Vimeo Video School comes out pretty much exactly like I said it should.

I am NOT saying that I in anyway deserve credit for these things, I am sure I had nothing to do with it. Just that I feel somewhat vindicated by my predictions coming to fruition.

And really I am writing this comment to mention an idea that has not yet come to pass: Vimeo Theater.

I predict that Vimeo will start holding independent and short film screenings in movie theaters or dedicated venues. It has the potential to be a huge social force, a unique theater-going experience with up-and-coming filmmakers holding Q&A's after the screening, and the rebirth of "traveling" films moving from city to city.

Indeed, something like Vimeo has the power to take filmmaking from its current studio-controlled industry to something more like indy music, with groups of filmmakers touring like bands do now.

That's my idea, anyway. I voiced this to Vimeo at least 3 years ago, we'll see if they ever get around to it.

There are quite a lot of services like this - Vimeo's one. Others include:

  • Gumroad - very good for sales but no way for people to browse, unlike Vimeo.
  • VHX - used by quite a few high-profile folk. I don't know much else about them.
  • Distrify - very nice player design for sales. Again, no way to browse, unlike Vimeo.

The killer issue with Vimeo On Demand for me is that it forces people to have a Vimeo account before they actually purchase. That's a pretty major roadblock, and I've read a few people saying that it kills conversion rates.

While the PPV is a great addition, it's not enough. Without an adsense type option they're only ever going to be a service for "serious" film makers and their only real income stream will be from Vimeo Pro subscription fees.
